title: 2027 Tax Planning Opportunities for Food & Beverage Businesses
summary: Unlock tax-saving opportunities for food and beverage. Explore strategies to improve cash flow, maximize deductions, and fuel growth.
body_markdown:
### Planning strategies for restaurants, beverage producers, food manufacturers, distributors, and emerging brands


Businesses in the[food and beverage](https://www.cbiz.com/industries/food-beverage) industry are entering 2027 with both familiar pressures and new planning opportunities. Rising labor costs, changing consumer preferences, supply chain challenges, and increased competition continue to affect margins. At the same time, recent tax legislation has created meaningful opportunities for companies willing to plan proactively. As businesses prepare for the year ahead, tax planning should move beyond annual compliance and become a tool to improve cash flow, support growth, and strengthen long-term enterprise value.


## Revisit Entity Structure Before Growth or Exit Events


Entity structure is one of the most important planning discussions. The permanent extension of the 20% qualified business income (QBI) deduction provides ongoing benefits for many partnerships, LLCs, S corporations, and sole proprietorships, while enhanced[Qualified Small Business Stock (QSBS](https://www.cbiz.com/services/tax/business-tax/qualified-small-business-stock) ) rules may make C corporations more attractive for companies with significant growth or exit potential. For owners contemplating acquisitions, private equity investment, or a future sale, revisiting entity choice could generate substantial tax savings over the life of the business.


## Use Capital Investment Planning to Improve Cash Flow


Many food and beverage businesses face ongoing needs for production equipment, refrigeration systems, packaging lines, point-of-sale technology, and facility improvements. The continued availability of 100% bonus depreciation and expanded Section 179 current deductibility allows eligible businesses to deduct the cost of many investments immediately rather than over several years. For manufacturers and processors, favorable treatment for certain production facilities may further enhance the economics of expansion projects.


## Look for Cash Flow Opportunities in Accounting Methods


Accounting methods continue to offer overlooked opportunities. Many businesses can improve cash flow through strategic timing of revenue and deductions, including evaluations of cash method eligibility, gift card income recognition, inventory methods, accrued compensation deductions, and small wares accounting. These opportunities can be particularly valuable for restaurants and food service operators that experience fluctuating margins and seasonal cash flow pressures.


## Capture Tax Benefits from Innovation


Innovation remains a significant source of tax benefits across the industry. While many companies do not view themselves as performing research and development, activities such as recipe development, beverage formulation, shelf-life improvements, packaging enhancements, production efficiency initiatives, and automation projects may qualify for favorable tax treatment. With the return of immediate deductions for qualifying domestic research expenditures, businesses should work closely with their advisors to identify and properly document qualifying activities.


**Planning example:** Consider a growing regional brewery that invests in a new canning line, implements production software to improve efficiency, and develops a new product line designed for broader distribution. By coordinating capital expenditure planning, evaluating potential research activities, and reviewing its entity structure, the company may be able to accelerate deductions, improve cash flow, and better position itself for future expansion or investment. While every business is different, this example illustrates how tax planning can directly support broader operational and strategic objectives rather than functioning as a year-end exercise.


## Do Not Overlook Labor, Payroll, and Tip Reporting


Restaurants and hospitality businesses continue to navigate changes affecting tip income, payroll administration, and employee reporting requirements. While recent legislation provides tax benefits to certain employees receiving tip income, employers should ensure systems and procedures remain aligned with ongoing reporting and compliance obligations. Effective payroll planning can help reduce administrative burdens while supporting employee retention efforts in an industry where labor remains one of the largest operating expenses.

## Plan for State and Local Tax Exposure


For businesses operating across multiple states, state and local tax planning is critical. Expansion through new locations, e-commerce sales, distribution networks, or acquisitions can create unexpected filing obligations and tax exposure. At the same time, many states continue to offer incentives for job creation, capital investment, and business expansion. Pass-through entity tax elections, nexus reviews, and state credit analyses should be part of every annual planning discussion.


## Prepare Early for Succession or Transactions


Finally, business owners should not overlook succession and transaction planning. Consolidation continues throughout the food and beverage sector, creating opportunities for strategic buyers, investors, and family-owned businesses considering liquidity events. Advance planning around tax basis, entity structure, state tax exposure, and estate considerations often has a direct impact on after-tax proceeds when a transaction occurs. The most successful exits typically begin years before a sale rather than months before closing.


## Make Tax Planning Part of the Business Strategy


The opportunities available in 2027 extend well beyond any single deduction or credit. Businesses that integrate tax planning into their broader operating strategy can often reinvest savings into technology, workforce initiatives, capacity expansion, or growth opportunities. In an industry where margins are frequently under pressure, a thoughtful tax strategy can provide a meaningful competitive advantage.


## Next Steps for 2027


As 2027 approaches, take the time to evaluate your current tax position, capital investment plans, multistate footprint, and ownership goals. Companies that begin planning early are often best positioned to maximize available tax benefits and navigate an increasingly complex business environment with confidence.

#### Frequently Asked Questions


Food and beverage companies can improve cash flow and reduce tax liability by focusing on proactive tax planning. Key strategies include evaluating entity structure, maximizing the 20% Qualified Business Income (QBI) deduction, leveraging Qualified Small Business Stock (QSBS) opportunities, and accelerating deductions through 100% bonus depreciation and Section 179 deductions. Restaurants, breweries, beverage producers, food manufacturers, and distributors should also review accounting methods, payroll processes, and multistate tax exposure.


Restaurants, food manufacturers, beverage producers, and distributors often invest heavily in equipment and facility improvements. Under current tax rules, eligible businesses may be able to immediately deduct qualifying purchases through 100% bonus depreciation and Section 179 expensing rather than depreciating them over multiple years. Common qualifying investments include production equipment, refrigeration systems, packaging lines, point-of-sale technology, automation systems, and facility upgrades. Furthermore, some food and beverage companies may qualify for the new Qualified Production Property 100% deduction for the cost of new buildings and associated real estate.
